post-hole-digger.context: Two long handles meeting at a hinge above a split spade shaped scoop. Used for fencing, deck building and planting jobs that need narrow deep holes dug by hand.

earth-auger.context: An engine powerhead with two side handles above a long spiral bit. Used to bore holes in the ground for fence posts, tree planting and ground anchors.

backhoe-loader.context: A wheeled tractor with a bucket on the front and a jointed digging arm at the back. Used for digging trenches, loading soil and general earthmoving on building sites.

wheel-loader.context: A four wheeled machine with a wide bucket raised on two lift arms. Used for loading gravel, sand and soil onto trucks and moving material on sites and in quarries.

skid-steer.context: A compact box shaped loader with a caged cab, small wheels and a front bucket on side arms. Used for landscaping, demolition clean up and work in tight spaces.

dump-truck.context: A truck in side view with its tipping bed raised at the back. Used to show haulage of gravel, soil and rubble, mining and construction transport.

articulated-dump-truck.context: An off road hauler with a separate cab and open body joined at a pivot, riding on large tyres. Used for mines, quarries and large earthmoving projects.

road-roller.context: A road roller with a large smooth drum at the front, a small cab and a rear wheel. Used for compacting asphalt, gravel and soil when building roads.

motor-grader.context: A long grading machine with a cab at the back, a long frame and a blade slung beneath. Used for levelling and shaping road surfaces and gravel tracks.

asphalt-paver.context: A low tracked machine with a hopper at the front and a wide screed at the back. Used for laying a smooth layer of hot asphalt on roads and car parks.

scissor-lift.context: A railed work platform raised on a crossed X frame above a wheeled base. Used for maintenance and construction work at height indoors and out.

boom-lift.context: A wheeled base with a long angled boom arm ending in a small railed basket. Used for reaching high places such as tree trimming, signage and building work.

telehandler.context: A four wheeled machine with a long telescopic boom and forks on the front. Used to lift pallets and building materials high up on construction sites and farms.

trencher.context: A tracked machine with a long angled digging chain boom reaching down behind it. Used for cutting narrow trenches for cables, pipes and drainage.

pile-driver.context: A tracked rig with a tall mast, a heavy hammer and a pile being driven into the ground. Used for building foundations, piers and sea walls.

concrete-pump-truck.context: A truck with a long folded jointed boom arm along its top and a hose at the tip. Used to pump wet concrete to floors and places a mixer truck cannot reach.

cement-truck.context: A truck carrying a large tilted drum that turns to keep concrete mixed. Used for delivering ready mixed concrete to building sites.

mobile-crane.context: A wheeled truck crane with the cab at the front and a long angled boom with a hook hanging from it. Used for lifting heavy loads on building sites and industrial jobs.

crawler-crane.context: A tracked crane with a cab on a wide base and a tall lattice boom with a hook on its cable. Used for very heavy lifts on large construction and energy projects.

mini-excavator.context: A small tracked digger with an open canopy cab, a bent boom and a bucket. Used for landscaping, small trenches and work in tight gardens.

wrecking-ball.context: A heavy steel ball swinging on a chain from the arm of a crane mast. Used for knocking down buildings, and as a symbol of demolition or destruction.

chain-hoist.context: A hoist body hanging from a top hook, with a loop of hand chain and a lower lifting hook. Used in workshops and garages to lift engines, machinery and heavy loads by hand.

winch.context: A cable drum between two side plates with a hand crank and a hook on the cable end. Used for pulling and lifting loads, vehicle recovery and boat trailers.

bottle-jack.context: A short upright hydraulic jack with a lift saddle on top, a pump socket on the side and a flat base. Used to raise cars, trucks and heavy equipment for repair.

floor-jack.context: A low wheeled trolley jack with a lifting arm, a round saddle and a long handle. Used in garages to lift a car quickly before placing axle stands.

scissor-jack.context: A diamond shaped screw jack with a threaded rod through the middle and flat pads at top and bottom. Carried in cars for changing a flat tyre.

jack-stand.context: A tripod axle stand with a notched centre post, a cup saddle on top and splayed legs. Used to hold a raised vehicle safely while working underneath.

engine-hoist.context: A folding workshop crane on wheels with a mast, a long boom, a hydraulic ram and a chain hook. Used to lift engines and gearboxes out of vehicles.

stack-light.context: Three stacked beacon segments with a domed top on a short pole and base. Used on factory machines to signal run, warning and fault states.

road-sweeper.context: A compact street cleaning truck with a hopper at the back and a bristled round brush at the front. Used for sweeping roads, car parks and building sites.

water-truck.context: A tank truck with a round tank and spray droplets at the rear. Used to damp dust on roads and building sites and to water large areas.

compact-track-loader.context: A small loader running on rubber tracks, with a caged cab and a front bucket on a short arm. Used for grading and loading on soft or muddy ground.

tunnel-boring-machine.context: Front view of a large round cutting wheel with spokes and a toothed rim. Used to show tunnelling for metros, roads, water and mining.

drilling-rig.context: A tall lattice derrick with cross bracing on a raised deck, with a drill pipe running down below. Used for oil and gas wells, water boreholes and mineral exploration.

traffic-barrel.context: A tall tapered drum with two reflective bands and a wide base ring. Used to channel traffic around road works and hazards.

jersey-barrier.context: End view of a concrete road barrier with a wide sloped base and a narrow top. Used to separate lanes and protect work zones on highways.

road-barricade.context: A horizontal striped board held up by two A frame legs. Used to close roads and footpaths and to mark a hazard or diversion.

caution-tape.context: A wavy ribbon with diagonal stripes stretched between two posts. Used to cordon off hazards, accident scenes and areas under construction.

road-work-sign.context: A warning triangle showing a figure digging with a shovel beside a mound. Used to warn drivers of roadworks and men at work ahead.

stop-slow-paddle.context: An octagonal sign on a short pole, the paddle held by traffic controllers to stop or slow vehicles. Used for temporary traffic control at road works.

construction-fence.context: A temporary mesh fence panel standing on two block feet. Used to secure building sites, events and open excavations.

dumpster.context: An open topped tapered waste container with a wide rim and vertical ribs. Used for building waste, renovations and commercial rubbish collection.

site-office-trailer.context: A long box shaped cabin standing on blocks with small windows and a door. Used as a temporary office, canteen or welfare unit on building sites.

warning-beacon.context: A domed flashing light on a small base with rays around it. Used on vehicles, machinery and sites to signal a hazard or work in progress.

sandbag-wall.context: A pyramid of filled sandbags laid in offset rows. Used for flood defence, blast protection and temporary barriers.

safety-net.context: A sagging rectangular net with a grid pattern hung between two poles. Used to catch falling people and debris on scaffolding and building sites.

debris-chute.context: A chain of stacked funnel shaped tubes leading down into a waste skip. Used to drop rubble safely from upper floors during demolition and renovation.

tarp.context: A flat rectangular sheet with grommet holes at the corners and one corner folded over. Used to cover loads, roofs, tents and equipment.

ratchet-strap.context: A load strap with a ratchet buckle in the middle and an open hook at each end. Used to tie down cargo on trucks, trailers and roof racks.

bungee-cord.context: A stretchy coiled elastic cord with a curled hook at each end. Used to hold luggage, tarps and loads in place.

fuel-jerry-can.context: A rectangular fuel can with a carrying handle on top, an embossed X and a pouring spout. Used to carry petrol, diesel or water.

first-aid-cabinet.context: A wall cabinet with a cross on the door and an eyewash bottle standing beside it. Used to mark first aid stations in workplaces and workshops.

blueprint-table.context: A tilted drafting table with a blueprint sheet laid out on its board. Used for architecture, engineering and technical drawing.

building-permit.context: A document with a folded corner, a solid house at the top and a round stamp at the bottom. Used for planning permission, building approval and licences.

demolition-site.context: A partly collapsed building with a jagged broken top and pieces of debris falling beside it. Used for demolition work, ruins and structural collapse.

excavation-pit.context: A cross section of a rectangular hole in the ground with a ladder standing in it. Used for trenches, foundation digs and groundwork.

foundation-footing.context: A cross section of an inverted T shaped concrete footing carrying a wall above the ground line. Used for building foundations and structural engineering.

safety-goggles.context: Wide single lens goggles with side vents and an elastic strap. Used in labs and workshops to protect eyes from splashes, dust and debris.

safety-glasses.context: Wraparound glasses with one curved lens and side shields. Used on building sites, in workshops and in labs to protect eyes from impacts.

ear-muffs-safety.context: Two large round ear cups joined by a headband arching over the top. Used to protect hearing from loud machinery, tools and shooting.

respirator-mask.context: A half face respirator with two round filter cartridges on the sides and a centre valve. Used when painting, sanding or working with dust, fumes and chemicals.

face-shield.context: A clear curved visor hanging down from a headband. Used to protect the face from splashes, sparks and flying particles while grinding or cutting.

safety-harness.context: A full body harness with shoulder straps, a chest ring, a waist strap and two leg loops. Used for work at height, climbing and fall arrest.

lanyard-hook.context: A short webbing lanyard with a large snap hook at each end. Used to tether a harness to an anchor point when working at height.

knee-pads.context: A padded knee cup with a strap on each side. Used by tilers, floor layers and gardeners to protect knees when kneeling.

steel-toe-boot.context: A work boot in side view with a thick sole and a rounded toe cap. Used as a symbol for safety footwear on building sites and in factories.

hard-hat-headlamp.context: A hard hat with a small lamp on the front and light rays shining upward. Used for mining, caving and night or underground work.

eyewash-station.context: Two water jets arcing up from a pair of nozzles over a small basin. Used in labs and workshops to flush chemicals from the eyes.

lockout-tag.context: A padlock with a large tag hanging beside it. Used to lock out and tag out machinery so it cannot be switched on during maintenance.

fall-arrest-block.context: A round self retracting lifeline housing with its cable and a hook hanging below. Used to arrest falls for people working at height.

cut-resistant-glove.context: A knit work glove with a cross hatched weave and a knife blade glancing off it. Used for kitchen, glass handling and sharp metal jobs.

welding-gloves.context: A long flared gauntlet glove with a thick seam across the palm. Used by welders, blacksmiths and foundry workers to protect hands from heat and sparks.

welding-apron.context: A heavy full length apron with a neck strap, waist ties and a pocket line, shown flat. Used by welders and blacksmiths to shield the body from sparks and heat.

safety-shower.context: An overhead shower head on a bent pipe with a pull ring hanging down and water drops below. Used in labs and factories to rinse off chemical spills.

ppe-kit.context: A hard hat, safety goggles and a glove grouped together. Used to mean protective equipment, safety gear or a safety induction kit.

fire-extinguisher.context: An upright cylinder extinguisher with a valve and squeeze lever on top and a hose curling down. Used to mark fire safety points and firefighting equipment.

fire-hose-reel.context: A wall mounted round reel with a spiral of coiled hose and a nozzle end hanging from the rim. Used to mark fire hose reels in buildings and workplaces.

site-hoarding.context: A tall solid panel wall with two posts rising above it and a door in the middle. Used to screen building sites from the street and keep the public out.
